newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Can says steel price increase to hurt earnings.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Can says steel price increase to hurt earnings.

text.p: U.S. Can Corp. said Wednesday that second-quarter earnings would be hurt by various factors and that it will take a third-quarter after-tax charge of $30 million to $35 million to restructure its business.

The manufacturer of steel and plastic containers said an extremely competitive pricing environment, steel cost increases and lower aerosol volumes will have an "adverse effect" on its second-quarter results.
In last year's second quarter, the company earned $5.1 million, or 39 cents a share, on sales of $180.6 million.
Despite the earnings warning, U.S. Can's stock posted the biggest percentage gain on the New York Stock Exchange on Wednesday, rising $2.375 to $15.375.
The Oak Brook, Ill.-based company said it hired Salomon Brothers Inc. to assist it in evaluating strategic alternatives.

U.S. Can said the total after-tax cost of the actions will come to approximately $14 million to $16 million, or $1.06 to $1.21 a share. It added that it expects annual after-tax cost savings of about $6 million, or 45 cents a share.

The company also announced that Chairman and Chief Executive Officer William Smith would retire effective June 30, 1998. Company directors have begun the search for a successor to Smith, who will remain a director after his retirement.
U.S. Can said the restructuring plan is aimed at making the company more efficient and will involve closing plants in Wisconsin, Illinois, Maryland, and Ohio, affecting more than 300 employees.

The company said it will discontinue its steel pail business, citing continued inroads by plastic products. As a result, it plans to sell its North Brunswick, N.J., facility. The closure will affect about $20 million in sales.
If it is unable to sell the facility, it will be closed, U.S. Can said, resulting in an after-tax charge of about $9.4 million.
The closure of its Racine, Wis., aerosol facility will cause U.S. Can to lose about $35 million in annual sales, the company said.

The four plant closures and organisational streamlining are expected to result in pretax charges of $35 million to $40 million, or $2.23 to $2.65 a share, with an after-tax cost of $11 million to $13 million.
